source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Valproate can cause fetal malformations and neurodevelopmental harm; effective contraception and pregnancy counseling are important.","B":"Valproate causes fetal harm only late in pregnancy; exposure around conception does not require special counseling.","C":"Folic acid completely eliminates valproate-related fetal risk, so additional pregnancy counseling is unnecessary.","D":"Valproate causes only mild reversible neonatal effects and is not associated with structural or cognitive harm."}}
source_row.rationale: Valproate exposure during pregnancy is associated with major congenital malformations, including neural-tube defects, and with decreased IQ and neurodevelopmental disorders. Labeling emphasizes effective contraception and counseling. Option A is correct; B, C, and D materially understate or mischaracterize the risk.
source_row.source_detail: Boxed Warning and Warnings and Precautions §5.4: fetal major congenital malformations including neural-tube defects, decreased IQ/neurodevelopmental disorders; effective contraception and regular counseling are advised when treatment is necessary. DailyMed prescribing information revised in 2026; current label live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: medication administration, adverse effects/interactions, reversal, monitoring and teaching. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
